title: Pixelation Retro Downscale Effect with Undo/Redo
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that implements a pixelation retro downscale post-processing effect with full undo/redo history.

SCENE SETUP:
- Create a scene with a perspective camera at position (0, 2, 5) looking at the origin.
- Add a directional light at (5, 10, 7) with intensity 1.0 and an ambient light with intensity 0.3.
- Place 3 objects in the scene: a red torus knot at (-2, 1, 0), a green icosahedron at (0, 1, 0), and a blue cylinder at (2, 1, 0). All objects should slowly rotate on their Y axis.
- Add a gray (#444444) ground plane at y=0, size 10x10.
- Render the scene to an offscreen render target at full resolution, then draw it to a second render target at a reduced resolution (pixelated), and finally draw that to the screen using a full-screen quad with nearest-neighbor (THREE.NearestFilter) sampling to achieve the blocky pixel look.

PIXELATION SYSTEM:
- The pixelation level is controlled by a 'pixelScale' factor (integer, range 1 to 16, default 4). A pixelScale of 1 means full resolution (no pixelation). A pixelScale of N means the intermediate render target is (screenWidth/N) x (screenHeight/N).
- The effective pixel block size in screen pixels equals pixelScale.
- When pixelScale changes, recreate the intermediate render target at the new reduced resolution.

UNDO/REDO HISTORY:
- Maintain an array 'history' that stores each pixelScale value when it is committed.
- Maintain a 'historyIndex' pointer into this array (0-based).
- Initial state: history = [4], historyIndex = 0.
- When the user changes pixelScale (via slider or keyboard), push the new value onto history (truncating any redo-able future states beyond historyIndex) and advance historyIndex.
- Ctrl+Z triggers Undo: move historyIndex back by 1 (if possible) and apply that pixelScale.
- Ctrl+Y triggers Redo: move historyIndex forward by 1 (if possible) and apply that pixelScale.
- The history array should store a maximum of 20 entries. If a new entry would exceed 20, remove the oldest entry and adjust historyIndex.

USER INTERACTIONS:
- A horizontal range slider (id='pixelSlider', min=1, max=16, step=1, initial value=4) to set pixelScale. Changing the slider commits a new history entry.
- Press ArrowUp to increase pixelScale by 1 (clamped to 16). Commits to history.
- Press ArrowDown to decrease pixelScale by 1 (clamped to 1). Commits to history.
- Press 'R' to reset pixelScale to 4 (commits to history).
- Ctrl+Z for undo, Ctrl+Y for redo (as described above).
- A toggle button (id='toggleEffect', text 'Toggle Effect') that enables/disables the pixelation post-process. When disabled, render at full resolution directly. The enabled/disabled state is tracked but NOT part of undo/redo history.

HUD / UI:
- Display a HUD overlay (id='hud') in the top-left corner showing:
  - Current pixelScale value (span id='hudPixelScale')
  - Effective resolution as WxH (span id='hudResolution')
  - History length (span id='hudHistoryLen')
  - History index (span id='hudHistoryIndex')
  - Effect enabled status (span id='hudEffectEnabled')
- Place the slider and toggle button in a control panel (id='controls') at the bottom center.

STATE MANAGEMENT:
- Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields updated every frame:
  - pixelScale: current integer pixelScale (1-16)
  - effectEnabled: boolean, whether pixelation is active
  - history: array of integers (the full history array)
  - historyIndex: integer (current index in history)
  - historyLength: integer (history.length)
  - canUndo: boolean (historyIndex > 0)
  - canRedo: boolean (historyIndex < historyLength - 1)
  - renderTargetWidth: integer, width of the intermediate render target (or full width if effect disabled)
  - renderTargetHeight: integer, height of the intermediate render target (or full height if effect disabled)
  - objectCount: integer, number of mesh objects in the scene (should be 4 including ground)
  - frameCount: integer, incremented each frame
  - sceneReady: boolean, true once first frame rendered
physics_constraints: pixelScale must be integer in [1,16]. Effective render target dimensions must equal floor(screenDim / pixelScale). History array length must never exceed 20. Undo/redo must not go out of bounds. Truncation on new commit after undo must discard future states.
